_source: Wu, 'When Errors Become Narratives: A Longitudinal Taxonomy of Silent Failures in a Production LLM Agent Runtime', arXiv:2606.14589v1, June 2026. Local copy: docs/amnesiac_institution/2606.14589v1.pdf (398,542 bytes, 18 pages). Extracted 2026-08-10 via the Read tool (H1 PASSES — PDF text extraction clean; pandoc fallback not needed).
_unit_rule: UNIT = Wu's INCIDENT, never the manifestation (pinned at extraction per the plan; Wu reports >=28 manifestations across 22 incidents). A multi-manifestation incident is coded on its primary mechanism as Wu presents it, with the manifestation count carried as metadata, never as extra units.
_coverage_gap: CRITICAL, discovered at extraction: the PDF does NOT contain 22 individually narrated incidents. Section 4 states 'Full per-incident detail is in the public catalog; here we ... narrate one or two representative incidents', and the Artifact Availability section confirms all 22 postmortems live in Wu's public system repository, which is NOT local. Per-class narrated-vs-total: A 1 incident narrated as 5 undifferentiated sub-events (of 1+6); B 3 of 4; C 4 of 5; D 4 of 4; E 5 of 8. Identifiable codeable units total 17, not 22. See _class_a_problem.
_class_a_problem: Wu's Table 1 gives Class A as '1 (+6)' — ONE incident with six sub-events. The paper narrates five environment quirks (bash 3.2 ERR traps; BSD awk on invalid UTF-8; absent GNU timeout; CJK full-width punctuation; ~4000-char message folding) and designates NONE as 'the incident'. Under the pinned incident-granularity rule Class A therefore yields exactly ONE unit, whose content is a list. It cannot support an expressibility verdict at any threshold: with n=1, the >=2/3 rule is decided by a single call. Pre-register Class A as VERDICT-INELIGIBLE rather than letting one coder call produce a class-level claim.
_redaction_rule: Direction (i) coders map these to OUR P1-P6, so every unit is stripped of Wu's taxonomy vocabulary: the class letters A-E and their names (environment/platform quirk, design-assumption mismatch, error swallowing, dilution, chained hallucination, fabrication, operational omission, forensic blind spot), 'fail-plausible', 'gray failure', and Wu's trigger/amplifier/concealer layer names. NOT redacted: the shared subject matter ('silent', 'never fired', 'green'), which belongs to neither taxonomy and whose removal would destroy the unit's codeability. Banned-lexicon list frozen in PREREGISTRATION.md.

units.symptom: A family of failures in which the code's logic was correct and the runtime environment's implicit behaviour defeated it. The development environment (Linux container, root, GNU userland, bash 5) is systematically more permissive than the production target (macOS, bash 3.2 as /bin/bash, BSD userland, zsh interactive shell, sandboxed cron).
units.mechanism_as_described: Recorded sub-events: bash 3.2 does not propagate ERR traps into functions without `set -E`, which disarmed a monitoring process's own self-alarm; BSD awk aborts on invalid UTF-8 multibyte sequences, which combined with `set -e` and `pipefail` to kill the monitoring script itself for seven days; the absence of GNU `timeout` on a stock host turned a defensive wrapper into a universal 'tool unavailable' failure; full-width CJK punctuation adjacent to unbraced shell variables parses as part of the variable name; and a messaging client folds long messages at an undocumented ~4,000-character threshold, changing the user-visible shape of every long push.
units.detection_path: Never visible in development, where everything stayed green; surfaced only on execution against the real target environment.
units.consequence: Silence lasting hours to weeks. A fix validated only in the development environment shipped broken twice in one day.
units.extraction_note: Wu narrates this class as one incident with six sub-events and designates no single exemplar. Unit content is therefore necessarily a list. VERDICT-INELIGIBLE at class level (n=1).

units.symptom: A component silently fell back to an unfiltered mode for five days, and a companion feature that was supposed to write health scores into shared state never executed at all.
units.mechanism_as_described: A metadata-resolution function shipped with three candidate paths for locating a registry file. All three missed the file's actual production location, because the deployment pipeline placed it under a path none of the candidates covered. The function's own log line announcing the fallback scrolled past unread.
units.detection_path: Unit tests were green throughout: they tested the resolution logic with fixtures laid out according to the same wrong assumption the code made.
units.consequence: Five days of unfiltered operation plus one feature that never ran.

units.symptom: Users received messages whose 'title' field contained a literal separator string.
units.mechanism_as_described: A parser consuming model output indexed lines positionally (line i+1, line i+2, stride 3). The model occasionally omits one line — instruction-following is a distribution, not a contract — after which every subsequent field shifted one slot.
units.detection_path: Caught by a human noticing malformed user-visible output; no automated check covered positional drift.
units.consequence: Systematically misassembled user-facing messages. Generalized afterwards into a standing rule that any positional parse of model output is a latent instance of this mechanism, plus a repository-wide check.

units.symptom: Production emitted three message windows where four were expected, while twelve tests passed.
units.mechanism_as_described: The test suite constructed its inputs with a heading format that the production caller never actually produces, so the tests exercised a shape reality did not supply.
units.detection_path: Discovered from user-visible output, not from the suite.
units.consequence: Wrong output shape in production with a fully green suite. Remedied with explicit cross-script contracts and deployment-layout testing on the real target.

units.symptom: A daily audit printed 'all invariants hold' while invariants were in fact raising exceptions.
units.mechanism_as_described: A summary function counted only results whose status field equalled 'fail'. Any invariant whose check raised an exception produced status 'error' instead, and those results were simply not counted by the summary.
units.detection_path: The observer had no observer; found only when the discrepancy was looked for directly.
units.consequence: A reassuring aggregate over a population that included uncounted failures.

units.symptom: Sixty-seven checks across twenty-one invariants passed continuously for months without ever executing any check logic.
units.mechanism_as_described: The executor read check code from one field of a configuration file, while those 67 checks had their code stored under a differently named field. The executor therefore evaluated an empty string for each of them, which succeeded every time.
units.detection_path: Discovered only when a newly added invariant was deliberately broken to confirm it would fire, and it refused to fail.
units.consequence: Months of vacuous passes indistinguishable, from the outside, from genuine passes.

units.symptom: A scheduled digest failed with 'HTTP 502 Bad Gateway' for two consecutive days, and the alert reaching the human contained no actionable information.
units.mechanism_as_described: The real cause — a fallback provider's free-tier quota exhausted by daytime jobs after the primary provider's circuit breaker had opened — was present in the upstream response body. The adapter wrapped that response into a 502; the proxy never read the body, capturing only the exception's string form; and the remnant the client finally received had been reduced to a formatted code-and-reason pair. Three hops, each individually reasonable, each stripping cause.
units.detection_path: A human read the alert and found it uninformative, then traced the chain by hand.
units.consequence: Two days of failure behind an alert with zero diagnostic content.

units.symptom: New validation logic was skipped in all eight job scripts it had just been added to, while every test and syntax check passed.
units.mechanism_as_described: An automated batch tool injected an environment-variable read into eight job scripts without injecting the corresponding import statement. Each of the eight raised a name-resolution error, which was caught by a fail-open guard that dutifully skipped the new validation logic. A single wrong design decision propagated to eight sites with machine efficiency, and the static syntax checker could not see inside the affected heredoc.
units.detection_path: Not caught by tests or syntax checking; found later by inspection.
units.consequence: Eight sites silently running without the validation that had just been installed.

units.symptom: A nightly synthesis job pushed a confident industry analysis about a platform crisis at a named company to the user. The crisis did not exist.
units.mechanism_as_described: Scraped content containing an isolated UTF-16 surrogate made a serialization call raise mid-write, producing a truncated request body and a 400 response carrying a small HTML error page. The map step's logging function wrote its diagnostics to standard output; the caller captured standard output as the signal payload; and the cache filled with error-code strings. The downstream model, prompted to find cross-domain signals, composed a fluent analysis around the most probable narrative shell for that error vocabulary. Every component behaved exactly as designed.
units.detection_path: No alarm of any kind. A non-empty check passed, a status file reported success, and no detector inspected content semantics. Discovered by the user noticing that the delivered analysis was thematically incoherent.
units.consequence: Counterfeit analysis delivered to a human as a routine insight digest. The load-bearing fix was a single output redirection operator.

units.symptom: Asked an unrelated architecture question, the system replied that it had 'received the system alert follow-up task' and instructed the user to grant a broad OS permission to a scheduled-job binary — instructions that were off-topic and technically invented for the scenario.
units.mechanism_as_described: An alert pushed by a monitoring process was persisted into the chat session history as an ordinary assistant message. Thirty-six minutes later, the model attending across that contaminated context wove the alert and the user's question into one narrative. Alert traffic and conversation are different speech acts; sharing one context window between them invites exactly this.
units.detection_path: Noticed by the user from the reply's irrelevance.
units.consequence: Fabricated remediation instructions delivered as guidance. Noted separately: weeks later an unrelated investigation established that the general direction the model had invented was coincidentally relevant to a real problem elsewhere — which does not make it grounded.

units.symptom: A weekly review artifact contained leftover container headings presented as if they were review content, and the job's status file recorded success unconditionally.
units.mechanism_as_described: The job's model call failed, and control fell back to a mechanical line-filter that emitted whatever text it found in the expected shape. The fallback then wrote a success flag into its status file regardless of outcome. Six co-located issues made the others harder to see.
units.detection_path: The artifact looked plausible enough to pass casual inspection for weeks; found on close reading.
units.consequence: Weeks of plausible-shaped but contentless output recorded as successful. Wu's own gloss: a fallback path that manufactures plausible-shaped output is the same failure implemented without a model.

units.symptom: A digest announced a community release of an internal version number that exists only in a changelog, attributing it to a source that never published it.
units.mechanism_as_described: Given a list of the day's high-alignment papers as context enrichment, the system inferred that the user's project 'must have shipped' and invented a source tag for the claim. The injected context was true but unlabelled: enrichment without provenance marking.
units.detection_path: Caught by the user recognizing their own version number.
units.consequence: False public-facing attribution generated from unlabelled true context.

units.symptom: A new daily-analysis job was fully implemented, tested, registered in the job registry, and deployed — and never ran once.
units.mechanism_as_described: The final installation step was a human memory item rather than an automated one, and three independent small bugs conspired to hide the omission: the preflight checker searched for only one of the two possible drift-warning strings; the install helper did not check its own exit code and compared counts with a less-than rather than an equality test, so it reported success on a rejected install; and the job's absence produced no log line for anything to scan.
units.detection_path: Nothing detected it; the absence produced no artifact to detect.
units.consequence: A completed, deployed feature that never executed. Generalized into the system's largest architectural correction: declared state must be reconciled to runtime state by machine rather than by memory.

units.symptom: For thirteen hours, every user message received a reply that arrived as nothing at all — total silence, with every component functioning exactly as designed.
units.mechanism_as_described: The agent, completing a task, wrote its notes into a file whose name it treated as an ordinary scratch filename. To the runtime, that filename is a reserved control file whose non-empty content activates a protocol instructing the model to reply with a bare acknowledgement token when nothing needs attention. The outbound gateway then strips that token from messages.
units.detection_path: Detected only by the human noticing they were receiving no replies.
units.consequence: Thirteen hours of total outbound silence. Remedied by making any path with special runtime semantics unwritable by the model's generic file tools.

units.symptom: An external-drive backup path failed with a permissions error and stayed broken for sixty days — the longest silence in the corpus.
units.mechanism_as_described: Six successive hypotheses (filesystem format, ownership identifiers, access-control lists, daemon contention, snapshot locks, physical disconnection) were each falsified by data over multiple weeks. The actual cause was an OS-level sandbox denying the scheduled process a permission class by default. The deeper problem was that during those weeks the diagnostic tools themselves — the process lister, the access-control lister, the snapshot enumerator — were being denied by the same sandbox and returning empty output, which the diagnosis pipeline recorded as 'normal' or 'empty'.
units.detection_path: Found only via the operating system's own audit log, which was the one instrument outside the sandbox.
units.consequence: Sixty days of broken backups plus weeks of investigation actively misled by its own instruments. Wu's gloss: an instrument that cannot distinguish 'nothing there' from 'I was not allowed to look' will manufacture false reassurance.

units.symptom: A nine-hour total gateway outage during which three independent alarms each failed to raise it.
units.mechanism_as_described: A quiet-hours filter suppressed both notification channels, including the one specifically designated for emergencies; a keepalive process logged a warning without alerting on it; and a restart script reported success without verifying that the restarted service was actually healthy.
units.detection_path: Detected by a human, after nine hours.
units.consequence: Nine hours of complete outage with three defences that each individually declined to fire. Generalized into a rule that an alert path must not depend on the failing subject.

units.symptom: A monitoring process died and stayed dead for seven days.
units.mechanism_as_described: The process was killed by an environment-level incompatibility in the runtime shell and text tooling, and nothing was watching the watcher — the monitoring layer had no independent observer of its own liveness.
units.detection_path: Not detected by anything automated; the monitoring layer's own silence was indistinguishable from a healthy quiet period.
units.consequence: Seven days with no monitoring at all. Remedied with self-alarms in the process plus an independently age-checked liveness file.
units.extraction_note: OVERLAP DECLARED: this incident shares its underlying event with two of WU-A1's sub-events (the ERR-trap self-alarm disarm and the seven-day text-tooling kill). Wu narrates it under both classes — as an environment quirk in one place and as a monitoring-layer omission in another. Kept as ONE unit here and flagged, so no duplicate enters the matrices; the cross-class overlap is itself reportable as evidence that Wu's classes are not mutually exclusive at incident granularity.
